messages:
maria: Heads-up — we're seeing sessions spike in the console during canary rollouts. Looks like early truncation + client reconnects generate retry storms and inflated provisional quota counts.

aj: Can you paste an example trace? is this streaming toolcall related or pure generation retries?

maria: Streaming toolcall. Client drops at ~token 512, reconnects, router issues a handoff which creates a new toolcall attempt. Billing shows both attempts as provisional and they both stick in the UI until finalization.

sujay: Oof. So the UI is summing provisional credits per attempt? That means short-lived retries double-count in dashboards.

maria: Exactly. The per-route quota graph + per-customer estimate shows a 2–3x bump for a minute during canary traffic.

taylor: Is the ledger recording attempt metadata (attempt_id / resume_offset)? If not, reconcile will be hard.

aj: Router currently tags attempts with `session_id` and `route_id`. No attempt-level id is surfaced to billing. We could add `X-Attempt-Id` on handoffs — small router change.

ben: Another idea: in the console we could smooth provisional spikes by deduping provisional credits that share `route_id` + `client_ip` + short time window. Cheap UX fix.

sujay: That sounds brittle. Client_ip isn't reliable (mobile NAT). We should prefer server-side dedupe using attempt_id when available, fallback to heuristics.

maria: Proposal: 1) expose `X-Attempt-Id` from router -> billing, 2) add `resume_offset` so we charge only delta tokens on resumed attempts, 3) console smoothing fallback for older data.

aj: Implementation notes: billing needs to treat provisional tokens as attach-to-attempt. On final confirmation, we sum unique token ranges per sessionid. If we receive resume_offset we can subtract overlap.

ben: UX: In the rollout dashboard show a toggle "Show deduped provisional credits" with a hover to explain the heuristic. Avoid surprising customers during canaries.

sujay: Telemetry: we should emit a metric `router.attempt_overlap_count` and `billing.provisional_dedupe_rate` to track how often the heuristic saves tokens.

maria: + add an alert when dedupe rate > 10% for > 5m during a rollout so we can pause canary.

aj: One edge: toolcalls with TTLs (short-lived tool sessions) — attempt_ids may be recycled quickly. Need globally unique id (uuid v4) and include `attempt_created_at` in proto.

taylor: Canary UX: when we flip a canary, console should show both raw provisional and deduped estimates side-by-side for 15m. That helps SREs decide if traffic is noisy.

ben: Who wants the router change? aj + sujay? I can do the console bits (toggle + graph).

aj: I can own router header change + instrument attempt_id/resume_offset. Need a spec for proto field names.

sujay: I'll update billing ingestion to accept `attempt_id` and `resume_offset` and implement the provisional dedupe using token-range set union. Will also emit the metrics.

maria: Deploy-bot: canary roll started on `api-canary-v12`

deploy-bot: api-canary-v12: deployment started by taylor at 2025-06-12T15:00:10Z :rocket:

maria: Action items: aj spec PR for headers by EOD, sujay billing ingestion change in this sprint, ben console toggle mock + small cohort test, taylor coordinate canary pause criteria.

ben: I'll mock the UI today and drop screenshots into the ticket.

aj: PR opened: router#678 — adds X-Attempt-Id, X-Resume-Offset headers. Comments welcome.

sujay: I'll draft billing ingestion change and a small backfill job to reconcile a day's worth of provisional duplicates so customers don't see weird spikes historically.

maria: Thanks all. Let's keep the canary on but watch `billing.provisional_dedupe_rate` and `console.quota_spike_pct`. If either crosses thresholds, pause. :thumbsup:
